newsitem.title: UK: Most rates will stay soft -U.S. insurer.
newsitem.headline: Most rates will stay soft -U.S. insurer.

text.p: Rates for most lines of insurance are set to remain soft indefinitely, a U.S. insurer told a conference on the London insurance market.

"I think it will continue to be soft unless the big one happens -- the earthquake or hurricane," Richard Bouhan, executive director of the National Association of Professional Surplus Lines offices, said on Wednesday.

"The market we're in now is the one that's here to stay," he said, noting that even a major hurricane, such as Andrew in 1992 which caused $15.5 billion of insured damage, had not been enough to push rates higher.
Bouhan was addressing a conference organised by the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU) and U.S. law firm Kroll & Tract.

The current soft insurance market was in part due to the strong performance of investment markets, which enabled insurers to make good overall profits, even while making an underwriting loss on their insurance business.
Surveys suggested U.S. insurers operated last year with combined ratios of 103-106 percent on average, losing three to six cents on each dollar of premium, he added.
Brokers reported firmer rates on a few lines of business, especially in niche markets such as taxi operators, but this did not alter the generally soft outlook, Bouhan said.
This view was echoed last week in a note from the London-based insurance analyst of Morgan Stanley.
"Premium rates, with very few exceptions, are generally falling around the globe, and no major upturn is expected in 1997," analyst Youssef Ziai said in a note on UK insurance brokers.
